schemes.notes: Partly verified. From the official BIIPP 2016 text: the subvention is 10% p.a., or the actual term-loan rate if lower, and 12% for micro and small units (para 6.2). It is paid in instalments linked to repayment and needs a term loan from a scheduled bank/RBI-SEBI-approved FI. Incentives end 5 years after commercial production starts (6.1(x)). The approved project cost caps land at 10% of other investment (6.1(vi)). Expansion/modernisation qualifies only with at least 50% capacity increase, on incremental project cost (6.1(xvii)). SC/ST, women, differently-abled, war widows, acid-attack victims and third gender: 13.8% for micro/small, 11.5% otherwise. The ORIGINAL 2016 caps were 30% (priority) / 15% (non-priority) of approved project cost, max Rs 10 crore (Rs 11.5 crore and 34.5%/17.25% for SC/ST/women). The caps in this record (50%/30%/15%; Rs 40/20/20 crore) are the BIIPP-2025 Option 1 values. They come ONLY from the MoFPI 'Compendium of state-specific schemes and incentives for food processing industry' (secondary) and the official BIIPP-2025 brochure (headline 'max up to 40 cr'). Rates are percentage points on the term loan, not a share of interest.

schemes.name: MIIPP 2024 State Capital Investment Incentive
schemes.authority: Government of Meghalaya (via District Industries Centre)
documents: Chartered Engineer certificate for plant & machinery
schemes.notes: 30% of P&M cost; cap Rs 10 crore Priority Sector, Rs 8 crore non-priority. New and expanding units, once per unit, one unit per applicant; physical verification. Min investment: manufacturing Rs 1 crore P&M (3.1.2); micro Rs 10 lakh in P&M + factory building (3.1.4 as amended 2025; building counts as P&M for micro, 3.1.5). Amendment 2025 (No.IND.15/2026/Pt/147, 09.12.2025) added 'Manufacturing (other than negative sectors)' to Priority Sectors (clause 2.4, item 21), so practically all eligible manufacturing units get Priority rates. Per amended para 5.1(ii) (Amendment 2025): where UNNATI 2024 or other GoI scheme overlaps, only the DIFFERENCE between State and GoI incentive is eligible. Since UNNATI CII is 30% (Zone A) / 50% (Zone B), state top-up is nil for most units; mainly useful where UNNATI cap (Rs 5/7.5 cr) is exceeded or unit is not UNNATI-registered. Registration window extended to 31.03.2027 (Notification No IND.15/2024/Pt.I/5 dated 10.09.2026). Max benefit per unit Rs 100 crore across all components.

schemes.authority: Government of India: Composite: Government of India schemes giving manufacturing MSMEs a computable cash benefit (Ministry of MSME + Department of Commerce/DGFT Export Promotion Mission). Each scheme's own source is given in its notes.
schemes.clause: Guidelines 2022 cl. 3.4.4 (cost), 3.4.5 (subsidy), 3.4.7 (surveillance); Addendum-1 dated Nov 2023 (women 100%, w.e.f. 11.11.2023); Addendum-2 dated 17.09.2024 (revised fees and surveillance, w.e.f. 18.09.2024)
schemes.notes: CHANGED from the figures we had before: Addendum-2 (No. 4/1/CLCS-TUS/PMAC/ZED-C/2020-21-Part(1), 17.09.2024, w.e.f. 18.09.2024) cut certification fees to Bronze Rs 8,000, Silver Rs 32,000 and Gold Rs 72,000. These fees include verification, assessment, certification, monitoring and taxes. The old fees of 10,000/40,000/90,000 are superseded. Bronze now also has a surveillance assessment at Rs 2,000 with 100% subsidy, and the Rs 2,000 balance of the joining reward covers it. Silver and Gold have 2 surveillance assessments, at Rs 10,000 and Rs 20,000, subsidised at 80/60/50%. The subsidy is 80/60/50% for micro/small/medium. Women-owned MSMEs get 100% (Addendum-1, w.e.f. 11.11.2023), and the extra 10% and 5% do not apply to them. Other units get an extra 10% if SC/ST-owned or located in NER, Himalayan, LWE, island territory or aspirational district, plus an extra 5% if they are part of SFURTI or MSE-CDP. The joining reward of Rs 10,000 is available once after the ZED Pledge and is valid for 1 year. The certificate is valid for 3 years. VALIDITY: Guidelines 2022 say 'valid till March 31, 2026'. On 12.03.2026 PIB said the scheme evaluation was 'under process'. The PIB Budget 2026-27 note and Ministry statements reported in Aug 2026 describe ZED as ongoing, but no official extension notice beyond 31.03.2026 was found. Sources: https://dcmsme.gov.in/Guidelines_MSME%20Sustainable(ZED)%20Certification%20Scheme.pdf ; https://dcmsme.gov.in/Addendum_1_Subsidy%20for%20Women%20Owned%20MSMEs%20under%20ZED.pdf ; https://dcmsme.gov.in/Addendum_2_Guidelines%20ZED%202.0.pdf . The dcmsme guideline web page still shows the OLD fees and is stale.
